title: The cycle C9 does not admit uniform mixing
authors: Alison Gray, Pransu Patel, Isaiah Young
abstract: We study continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on cycles. In particular, we prove that the cycle $C_9$ does not admit uniform mixing at any time via algebraic geometry and Gröbner basis techniques to rule out all cyclic 9-roots.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that continuous-time quantum walks on the cycle graph $C_9$ never reach a state of uniform mixing at any time. The proof relies on sophisticated algebraic geometry techniques applied to the system's evolution operator, demonstrating an inherent mathematical impossibility for such mixing to occur.
main_problem: The study aims to prove mathematically whether the cycle graph $C_9$ admits uniform mixing for continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) at any time $t$.
main_result: The authors prove, using algebraic techniques, that the cycle $C_9$ never exhibits uniform mixing for CTQWs because the necessary conditions lead to contradictions regarding the nature of the required time parameter.
method: The analysis employs advanced mathematical tools including algebraic geometry and Gröbner basis techniques applied to cyclic roots, comparing derived matrix structures with the system's transition matrix.
model_or_system: The physical model is a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) evolving on the cycle graph $C_9$. Uniform mixing requires that all entries of the time evolution operator $U(t)$ have a squared magnitude of $1/n$ at time $t$.
key_observables: The primary observable is the transition matrix $U(t) = e^{itA(G)}$, and the diagnostic is whether its elements achieve uniform magnitude ($1/n$).
important_parameters: The cycle size $n=9$, and the time parameter $t$ (or related parameters $	au$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that if uniform mixing occurs, specific algebraic relationships must hold between eigenvalues derived from the system's structure.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the necessary conditions for uniform mixing, converting these into algebraic constraints involving cyclic $n$-roots, and then using contradiction via Gröbner bases to rule out solutions for $C_9$.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing quantum transport phenomena on lattices, which is highly relevant to understanding decoherence and mixing in open quantum systems.
